en: Vedavyasa said: Om. Of this great mantra, the divine hymn of the thousand names of Vishnu:
The seer is the revered Vedavyasa. The metre is Anushtup. The deity is the great Vishnu, the Supreme Self, Shriman Narayana. The seed is 'Amritamshudbhava Bhanu'.
The power is 'Devakinandana Srashta'. The highest mantra is 'Udbhava Kshobhana Deva'. The pin (kilaka) is 'Shankhabhrit Nandaki Chakri'. The weapon is 'Sharngadhanva Gadadhara'.
The eye is 'Rathangapani Akshobhya'. The armour is 'Trisama Samaga Sama'. The source is 'Ananda Parabrahma'. The binding of the directions is 'Ritu Sudarshana Kala'.
The meditation is 'Shri Vishvarupa'. This repetition of the thousand names is done to please the great Vishnu.

Om. On the head: salutation to the seer Vedavyasa. On the mouth: salutation to the Anushtup metre. In the heart: salutation to the deity Krishna, the Supreme Self. On the private parts: salutation to the seed 'Amritamshudbhava Bhanu'.
On the feet: salutation to the power 'Devakinandana Srashta'. On the whole body: salutation to the pin 'Shankhabhrit Nandaki Chakri'. With joined palms: I use this repetition to please Lord Krishna.
Thus ends the placing of the seer and the others on the body.

Om. With 'Vishvam Vishnur Vashatkara': salutation to the thumbs. With 'Amritamshudbhava Bhanu': to the index fingers. With 'Brahmanyo Brahmakrid Brahma': to the middle fingers. With 'Suvarnabindur Akshobhya': to the ring fingers.
With 'Nimisho Animishah Sragvi': salutation to the little fingers. With 'Rathangapani Akshobhya': to the palms and backs of the hands. Thus ends the placing on the hands.

first: ॐ विश्वं विष्णुर्वषट्कार इति हृदयाय नमः।
en: Om. With 'Vishvam Vishnur Vashatkara': salutation to the heart. With 'Amritamshudbhava Bhanu': svaha to the head. With 'Brahmanyo Brahmakrid Brahma': vashat to the tuft of hair. With 'Suvarnabindur Akshobhya': hum to the armour.
With 'Nimisho Animishah Sragvi': vaushat to the three eyes. With 'Rathangapani Akshobhya': phat to the weapon. Thus ends the placing on the six limbs.
The resolve: 'To please Lord Krishna, I will now repeat the divine thousand names of Vishnu.'
